title: Stimulating Consumption at Low Budget – Evidence from a Large-Scale Policy Experiment Amid the COVID-19 Pandemic
authors: Qiao Liu; Qiaowei Shen; Zhenghua Li; Shu Chen
eligible_reason: Not a staggered TWFE design. Each coupon wave is analyzed separately: coupon receivers vs users who failed to claim on the same day, with one common post (redemption) period per wave. Regressions are pooled OLS without unit or time fixed effects (felm(pay_amt ~ coupon + post + coupon:post + user_age + user_age2 + user_gender + pay_amt_3up + pay_amt6m | 0 | 0 | user_id), code for coupon.R), with individual covariates in every column. Matched samples (d_matched) and week-by-week post dummies (post1..post5) keep a single date per wave.
design_notes: R lfe::felm. Alipay user x week panels per wave (100k treated, 100k failed claimants). Outcomes: total, offline, online and category spending. Survey analysis in Stata (appendix).
n_adoption_cohorts_note: Single redemption period within each wave; waves estimated separately, never pooled with wave-specific dates.
data_files_note: ReadMe: Sample_data.csv is a synthetic 200-row dataset ('not real data and does not replicate our results'); Alipay data under NDA. Only the appendix survey data are real.
data_provenance_note: Main-results data are synthetic; real transaction data not shipped.
screener_notes: Screened from package only (no article text or PDF). Randomized-like coupon lottery with one date per wave and no FE; not staggered; synthetic sample data only.
